classification.difficultyReason: Represent the bearing as a southeast right triangle, find the angle from south and select cosine to calculate the southward component.

content.prompt: A plane flies on a bearing of $142^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$ for 400 km. How far south of its starting point is the plane now? (Give your answer in kilometres, correct to 1 decimal place.)

answer.worked:
The flight direction makes an angle of $180^{\circ}-142^{\circ}=38^{\circ}$ with south. Let $s$ be the distance south, in kilometres.

$$\begin{align*}\cos 38^{\circ}&=\frac{s}{400}\\s&=400\cos 38^{\circ}\\s&\approx315.2\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

The plane is 315.2 km south of its starting point.
